frontier.hypothesis: An ordinary-C reference to the end pointer placed in block_5c or block_6c - the two blocks reached immediately after the inner loop's last use of it - raises allocno 78 to 6 refs while keeping live_length at 10 or 11, landing inside (10434, 13500) and closing the function.
frontier.mechanism: vG proved cse1 does not fold a cross-block re-mention of var_t0 (78 went 4 refs -> 6 refs, weight 2 per flow.c:434 / flow.c:2081). vG failed only on distance: block_74 stretches live_length to 14 (pri 8571). block_5c sits 2-3 insns past the slt, so the same +2 refs there gives pri 12000 (live 10) or 10909 (live 11), both inside the window. Pair it with the free declaration-order swap (memory/grind/func_80037B00/decl_order_swap_vC.c) so that even an exact tie seats the end pointer first.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate spellings that mention var_t0 once in block_5c / block_6c while keeping the stream at 36 instructions in target's order - the candidate consumers are the 'var_t1 += 1' / 'var_t2 = 1' statements and the two exit arms. Splice with tmp/grind/func_80037B00/s9/apply.py, screen FIRST with tmp/grind/func_80037B00/s9/probe.sh (it prints the .lreg banner and the cc1 assembly in one call, no sandbox needed), accept only rows where 78 shows refs 6 and live <= 11 AND the cc1 stream is unchanged, then confirm with '& tools/wteng.ps1 main sandbox func_80037B00 --disable all'. POLICY BOUNDARY before spelling: a re-store of a local for its own sake is the dead-store family (FAKE-gated, .claude/rules/dead-store-fake-exception.md) - look first for a spelling where the mention is the function's own logic (e.g. an exit arm that legitimately consumes the end pointer).

frontier.hypothesis: The (refs 4, live 6) / (4,7) row - same refs, live range 2-3 insns SHORTER - is reachable by making the end pointer's definition later in the PRE-COMBINE insn order while the final scheduled stream keeps 'addiu $t0,$a3,0x15' as the fourth insn of the loop head.
frontier.mechanism: reg_live_length is computed by flow's life_analysis on the pre-combine, pre-sched stream (toplev.c order: flow -> combine -> sched1 -> local_alloc), so it measures the RTL order cc1 emitted, not the order the scheduler finally prints. Any spelling whose expansion emits the end-pointer definition closer to the slt shortens live_length without touching the emitted stream, and (4,7) alone gives pri 11428 > 10434.
frontier.next_probe: Read tmp/grind/func_80037B00/s9/flow.rtl (allocno 78 spans insn 46 to insn 82) and identify exactly which insns flow counts inside the span; then try loop-head statement orders and expression spellings that move the definition of var_t0 down the RTL while sched1 restores target's order. frontier.hypothesis: If neither row is reachable at 36 instructions, the residual is a chassis property rather than a spelling property: a DIFFERENT source shape that emits the same 36 instructions but with different block boundaries would move both live lengths at once.
